taxonomic_note: Legacy Master Plant Pool name Chamaesyce prostrata is normalized to the current accepted Euphorbia name.
look_here_first: First ask whether the stems form a true rooted mat. E. prostrata is prostrate to decumbent but usually does not form the tightly rooting mat of E. serpens. Then inspect the fruit: the capsule is characteristically crisped-villous along the keels and toward the base. Mature seeds are sharply 4-angled with several narrow transverse ridges.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays-local legacy Chamaesyce source; current Kew explicitly treats Chamaesyce prostrata as a synonym of accepted Euphorbia prostrata Aiton.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Installed for active visual learning; broader exact-county reconciliation deferred.

morphology_keys.family_pattern: Euphorbia sect. Anisophyllum sandmat: opposite leaves, milky latex, tiny axillary cyathia, and a 3-lobed capsule; hair placement, stipules, capsule pubescence, and seed sculpture are high-value characters.
morphology_keys.growth_form: Annual with taproot; stems prostrate to decumbent, about 10–30 cm, usually not forming a tightly rooted mat.
morphology_keys.stems: Stems crisped-villous to nearly glabrous proximally; hairs are much more evident than in the essentially glabrous E. serpens.
morphology_keys.leaves: Opposite; blades broadly elliptic to elliptic-oblong, ovate-spatulate, or ovate, usually about 3–11(–15) × 3–6(–8) mm; base slightly asymmetric and rounded to slightly cordate/oblique; margins serrulate at least distally.
morphology_keys.stipules: Triangular-subulate; connate on the lower side of the stem or distinct on the upper side, often lacerate distally.
morphology_keys.cyathium: Cyathia solitary or in small cymose clusters; 4 reddish glands with rudimentary white-to-pink appendages.
morphology_keys.fruit: Capsule broadly ovoid, about 1.2–2 × 1.4–1.5 mm; crisped-villous along the keels and toward the base, often glabrous between the keels.
morphology_keys.seed: Seeds about 0.8–1.1 × 0.5–0.7 mm, sharply 4-angled in cross section, with several narrow, sharp, slightly irregular transverse ridges.
best_field_traits: prostrate/decumbent annual but usually not a tightly rooting mat
crisped-villous stems and lower leaf surfaces
serrulate leaves with slightly asymmetric bases
capsule hairs concentrated along keels and toward base
sharply 4-angled seeds with narrow transverse ridges
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Against E. serpens: prostrata is coarser and hairy, usually not rooted into a tight mat, with serrulate leaves and hairy capsule keels. E. serpens is glabrous, roots at nodes, has tiny entire rounded leaves, glabrous capsules, and smooth seeds. Against E. villifera: prostrata stays more strictly prostrate and has capsule pubescence; villifera is typically erect/ascending and conspicuously villous over stems and leaf surfaces but has glabrous capsules.

lookalike_matrix.Euphorbia prostrata: prostrate to decumbent; usually not a tightly rooting mat
lookalike_matrix.Euphorbia serpens: strictly prostrate, frequently mat-forming and rooting at nodes
lookalike_matrix.Euphorbia villifera: usually erect to ascending, rarely prostrate

lookalike_matrix.Euphorbia prostrata: crisped-villous on stems/abaxial leaves; fruit hairy on keels
lookalike_matrix.Euphorbia villifera: usually conspicuously villous over stems and leaves
weakly 4-angled; smooth/faintly rugose or inconspicuously ridged

comparisons.key_distinctions: The fastest confirmation is the fruit: hairy capsule keels strongly favor E. prostrata over E. serpens and E. villifera. Seed ridges provide a second excellent check.
